mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar pre-announced rate hike periods (p > 0.10 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 6-month window, the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE changes and SPX 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: During periods of similar INDPRO momentum, SPX 5-day forward returns are not higher than average (median ratio < 1.02).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces policy uncertainty, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days in a low-inflation environment.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In deflationary regimes similar to the current one, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during prior CPIAUCSL < 3% periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential mortgage applications (HOUST) falls by more than 10% for two consecutive months, it indicates cooling credit demand and a higher probability of rate cuts, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by > 10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During analogous HOUST declines, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher (median ratio < 1.015).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in layoffs (indirect proxy via UNRATE) suggests a tight labor market that can drive equity valuations higher, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE remains flat or declines
failure_condition: In periods of similar PAYEMS/UNRATE dynamics, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales volume (implied via GDPC1 quarterly trend) followed by a rebound exceeding 2% in the next quarter is interpreted as a bottoming-out signal, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During analogous GDPC1 rebound phases, the 60-day forward return is not higher than historical averages (mean ratio < 1.015).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2.5%, it reduces policy uncertainty and often precedes a period of higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns as markets price in lower future rate hikes.
failure_condition: In regimes with similar low inflation, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during prior low-inflation periods (p > 0.10).
